issues.current: National median aide wage $17.21/hr is used for every Georgia configuration. The notes say the Georgia statewide aide wage was not retrieved.
issues.correct: Secondary compilations of BLS OEWS May 2025 list the Georgia median for home health and personal care aides at about $29,270/yr, or $14.07/hr. The national figure is verified at $17.21. I could not confirm the Georgia figure on bls.gov directly.
issues.evidence: careslink.com (BLS May 2025 state table): 'Georgia | $29,270 | $14.07'. BLS OOH: 'median annual wage ... $35,800 in May 2025'.
issues.fix: Pull the Georgia state OEWS May 2025 value for SOC 31-1120 (and the Atlanta MSA value) from bls.gov/oes. Replace $17.21 with that value, or show it as a sensitivity case. At about $3/hr lower, a 730-hr/month aide line is roughly $2,300/month cheaper. Keep $17.21 only if you label it a deliberately conservative national proxy.

issues.current: Overall national aide median $35,800 ($17.21/hr) is used for assisted living aides.

issues.fix: If a national wage is kept, use the industry-specific $37,060 ÷ 2,080 = $17.82/hr and note that it is national. The $17.21 figure is the all-industry median.

issues.fix: Add the ALC exceptions, or state that 18 is the safe floor for both ALC and PCH. Reword 'direct-care supervisory staff' to 'on-site manager and responsible staff persons'.

issues.evidence: The 1:15 / 1:25 PCH ratios in S32/S33 could not be re-checked because the rule-text fetch was blocked. 730 hrs = 24 × 30.42 and 1,216.8 = 40 × 30.42, so the arithmetic is correct.
